newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Fairfax sees 1st half on budget.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Fairfax sees 1st half on budget.

text.p: Newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday that its first half results in the current 1996/97 year should be in line with its budget.
"The first half, I think we should track with budget," Fairfax chief executive Bob Muscat told reporters after the company's annual meeting.
Muscat did not say what the company was budgeting for in the first half and would not comment on the company's first quarter results, which he said would be released in the next couple of weeks.
Fairfax chairman Sir Laurence Street said earlier the slower Australian economy coupled with higher newsprint prices will impact upon the group's final results for the year to June 30, 1997.
Fairfax said early last month it experienced a flat first quarter and expected similar conditions for the rest of 1996/97.
Fairfax reported a net profit of A$62.43 million for the six months to December 31, 1995 from A$81.26 million in the previous corresponding half.
Fairfax reported a 29.8 percent drop in net profit before abnormals to A$101.5 million for the 1995/96 year.
Conrad Black's Hollinger International Inc owns 25 percent of Fairfax, while Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd holds 15 percent and Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd owns five percent.
